scope: Proposition 3.3 (Buffered circuits and attached-wall bounds) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix positive aspect and buffer ratios. There are p > 0 and a fixed lattice cutoff c∗ > 0 with the following properties, uniformly for every physical test radius r ≥ c∗δ and every mesh. Test neighborhoods must lie in the ambient domain, apart from matching cell regions to which one of the preceding completion rules applies. 1. In a buffer containing no pins, a circuit of either prescribed W color in a fixed-aspect annulus has probability at least p, conditional on arbitrary admissible (s, W) data outside the buffer. Compatible pins of the requested color inside the buffer only improve the bound. Finite chains of overlapping circuit tests give a positive lower bound for a fixed-aspect tube connection. 2. After any admissible (s, W) stopping exploration, failure of matching circuits on m separated available scales has probability at most (1 − p)m, when each scale is chosen from the current history before its interior is examined. In particular, suppose a prescribed connected matching wall reaches from B(z, r) to outside B(z, R), with a fixed buffer around B(z, R). A path avoiding that wall and all attached matching circuits, and joining B(z, r) to outside B(z, R), has probability at most C  r + δ R α (3.8) for some C, α > 0. 3. When a test buffer meets F, the circuit and tube events mean circuits and connections in the augmented matching graph just defined. They have the same lower bounds under the exact completion of one component or the exact completion with a common fill. A circuit attached to F blocks an accessible dual path by its actual part together with the forbidden region F. If only the k-label comparison is available, the probability bounds lose at most 2O(k) in total. The number of local entrances of one label does not enter this cost. The bulk assertion in item 1 also holds before removing the model’s single wired N component. Conditioning in a search concerns (s, W); an exact cut history with exterior colors is allowed because its accessible marginal is already a fresh flat kernel.
